tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the band say he never really understood?

options.A: Why Roman Holiday was more famous than Breakfast at Tiffany's.
options.B: Why Audrey Hepburn had more female fans than male ones.
options.C: Why the woman wanted to be like Audrey Hepburn.
options.D: Why so many girls adored Audrey Hepburn.

questions.cn: 男士说他始终不太明白的是什么？

optionsCn.A: 为什么《罗马假日》比《蒂凡尼的早餐》更有名。
optionsCn.B: 为什么奥黛丽·赫本的女性粉丝比男性多。
optionsCn.C: 为什么女士想成为奥黛丽·赫本那样的人。
optionsCn.D: 为什么那么多女孩崇拜奥黛丽·赫本。

questions.stem: What prevented Audrey Hepburn from becoming a professional dancer?

options.A: Her unique personality.
options.B: Her physical condition.
options.C: Her shift of interest to performing arts.
options.D: Her family's suspension of financial aid.

questions.cn: 是什么让奥黛丽·赫本没能成为职业舞者？

optionsCn.A: 她独特的个性。
optionsCn.B: 她的身体状况。
optionsCn.C: 她的兴趣转向了表演艺术。
optionsCn.D: 她家人中断了经济支持。

questions.stem: What do we learn about Audrey Hepburn in real life?

options.A: She was not an outgoing person.
options.B: She was modest and hardworking.
options.C: She was easy-going on the whole.
options.D: She was usually not very optimistic.

questions.cn: 关于现实生活中的奥黛丽·赫本，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 她不是个外向的人。
optionsCn.B: 她谦逊而勤奋。
optionsCn.C: 她总体上随和。
optionsCn.D: 她通常不太乐观。

questions.stem: Why did Audrey Hepburn devote much of her life to charity after her acting career?

options.A: She was influenced by the roles she played in the films.
options.B: Her parents taught her to symbolize with the needy.
options.C: She learned to volunteer when she was a child.
options.D: Her family benefited from other people's help.

questions.cn: 为什么奥黛丽·赫本在演艺生涯结束后把大半生投入慈善？

optionsCn.A: 她受到自己所演电影角色的影响。
optionsCn.B: 她父母教她要同情穷人。
optionsCn.C: 她小时候就学会了做志愿服务。
optionsCn.D: 她的家人曾得到过别人的帮助。

lines.t: Conversation 1.
lines.cn: 对话一。

lines.t: F: Wow, I would give anything to be more like Audrey Hepburn.
lines.cn: F：哇，我愿意付出一切，只为更像奥黛丽·赫本一些。

lines.t: M: I never really understood why so many girls were such big fans of her.
lines.cn: M：我一直不太理解，为什么这么多女孩都是她的铁杆粉丝。

lines.t: M: I mean, I've seen the famous films, Roman Holiday, Breakfast at Tiffany's, and a few others, but I still don't fully get it.
lines.cn: M：我是说，那些有名的电影我都看过——《罗马假日》《蒂凡尼的早餐》，还有另外几部——可我还是没能完全明白。

lines.t: M: Was she that great of an actress?
lines.cn: M：她的演技真有那么出色吗？

lines.t: F: Well, for me, my adoration goes beyond her movies.
lines.cn: F：嗯，对我来说，我对她的喜爱不止于她的电影。

lines.t: F: She had such a classic elegance about her.
lines.cn: F：她身上有一种经典的优雅气质。

lines.t: F: She was always so poised, in part because she spent years training as a ballet dancer before becoming an actress.
lines.cn: F：她总是那么端庄从容，部分原因是她在成为演员之前，花了多年时间接受芭蕾舞训练。

lines.t: M: Why didn't she stick to dancing as a career?
lines.cn: M：她为什么没有把舞蹈坚持下去当职业呢？

lines.t: F: It seems it was fate.
lines.cn: F：看来是命运使然。

lines.t: F: She suffered from inadequate nutrition during the war, and therefore a career as a professional dancer would have been too demanding on her body.
lines.cn: F：她在战争期间营养不良，因此职业舞者这条路对她的身体来说负担太重了。

lines.t: F: So she focused on acting instead.
lines.cn: F：于是她转而专注于表演。

lines.t: F: Roman Holiday was her first big break which made her a star.
lines.cn: F：《罗马假日》是她第一个重大机遇，让她成了明星。

lines.t: M: Was that the film that opened with her shopping for jewelry in New York City?
lines.cn: M：就是那部开头她在纽约买珠宝的电影吗？

lines.t: M: You know, the scene she was wearing a black dress and dark sunglasses with a pearl necklace and long black gloves?
lines.cn: M：你知道的，就是她穿着黑裙、戴着墨镜、配着珍珠项链和黑色长手套的那一幕？

lines.t: M: I see the photo of her in that costume everywhere.
lines.cn: M：她那身装扮的照片我到处都能看到。

lines.t: F: No, that one is Breakfast at Tiffany's.
lines.cn: F：不是，那是《蒂凡尼的早餐》。

lines.t: F: That costume is often referred to as the most famous little black dress of all time.
lines.cn: F：那身装扮常被称为史上最著名的小黑裙。

lines.t: F: Her character in that film is very outgoing and charming, even though in real life, Audrey always described herself as shy and quiet.
lines.cn: F：她在片中饰演的角色非常外向迷人，尽管在现实生活中，奥黛丽总说自己害羞又安静。

lines.t: M: So what did she do after her acting career?
lines.cn: M：那她结束演艺生涯之后做了什么？

lines.t: F: She dedicated much of her life to helping children in need.
lines.cn: F：她把人生的大部分时间献给了帮助贫困儿童。

lines.t: F: Her family received international aid during the war when she was growing up.
lines.cn: F：她成长期间，家人曾在战争中接受过国际援助。

lines.t: F: I think that left a big impression on her.
lines.cn: F：我想那件事给她留下了很深的印象。

lines.t: F: That's where I got the idea to volunteer for children's charity next weekend.
lines.cn: F：我也因此想到，下周末去参加儿童慈善活动的志愿服务。

lines.t: M: I'll join you.
lines.cn: M：我跟你一起去。

lines.t: M: I may not be as charming as Audrey Hepburn, but I'm all for supporting a good cause.
lines.cn: M：我可能没有奥黛丽·赫本那么迷人，但我完全支持做点善事。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What is the man going to do?

options.A: Give a presentation.
options.B: Raise some questions.
options.C: Start a new company.
options.D: Attend a board meeting.

questions.cn: 男士打算做什么？

optionsCn.A: 做一场演示。
optionsCn.B: 提出一些问题。
optionsCn.C: 创办一家新公司。
optionsCn.D: 参加董事会会议。

questions.stem: What does the man say about the restructuring?

options.A: It will cut production costs.
options.B: It will raise productivity.
options.C: No staff will be dismissed.
options.D: No new staff will be hired.

questions.cn: 关于重组，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它将降低生产成本。
optionsCn.B: 它将提高生产率。
optionsCn.C: 不会有员工被解雇。
optionsCn.D: 不会招聘新员工。

questions.stem: What will the man explain first?

options.A: The timeline of restructuring.
options.B: The reasons for restructuring.
options.C: The communication channels.
options.D: The company's new missions.

questions.cn: 男士会先解释什么？

optionsCn.A: 重组的时间安排。
optionsCn.B: 重组的原因。
optionsCn.C: 沟通渠道。
optionsCn.D: 公司的新使命。

questions.stem: How can the staff learn more about the company's restructuring?

options.A: By consulting their own department managers.
options.B: By emailing questions to the man or the woman.
options.C: By exploring various channels of communication.
options.D: By visiting the company's own computer network.

questions.cn: 员工怎样才能了解更多关于公司重组的信息？

optionsCn.A: 向自己部门的经理咨询。
optionsCn.B: 把问题发邮件给男士或女士。
optionsCn.C: 探索各种沟通渠道。
optionsCn.D: 访问公司自己的内部网络。

lines.t: Conversation 2.
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: F: So, how's our presentation about the restructuring of the company coming along?
lines.cn: F：那么，我们那个关于公司重组的演示准备得怎么样了？

lines.t: M: Fine.
lines.cn: M：还好。

lines.t: M: I'm putting the finishing touches to it now, but we'll have to be prepared for questions.
lines.cn: M：我正在做最后的润色，不过我们得准备好回答问题。

lines.t: F: Yes, there's already a feeling that this is a top-down change.
lines.cn: F：是啊，已经有人觉得这是一次自上而下的变动。

lines.t: F: We really need to get everyone on board.
lines.cn: F：我们真的需要让所有人都参与进来。

lines.t: M: Well, there's been an extensive consultation period.
lines.cn: M：嗯，我们经过了长时间的广泛磋商。

lines.t: F: I know, but there's always the feeling that if it isn't broke, don't fix it.
lines.cn: F：我知道，但大家总有那种“没坏就别修”的想法。

lines.t: F: People are worried about their jobs, too.
lines.cn: F：人们也在担心自己的工作。

lines.t: M: I think we need to stress that while there'll be some job changes, there won't be anyone getting dismissed.
lines.cn: M：我觉得我们得强调，虽然岗位会有一些变化，但不会有人被解雇。

lines.t: M: In fact, we're looking to take on more staff.
lines.cn: M：事实上，我们还打算再招更多的人。

lines.t: F: Agreed.
lines.cn: F：同意。

lines.t: F: You can hardly blame people for worrying, though.
lines.cn: F：不过话说回来，也怪不得大家会担心。

lines.t: M: We need to make it clear that it's not just change for change's sake.
lines.cn: M：我们要说明清楚，这不是为了变而变。

lines.t: M: In other words, we really must make the case for why we are doing it.
lines.cn: M：换句话说，我们必须把为什么要这么做讲透。

lines.t: F: So, what's the outline of the presentation?
lines.cn: F：那演示的大纲是怎样的？

lines.t: M: I'll start with a brief review of the reasons for the change, that we really need to make a clean break to restart growth.
lines.cn: M：我开头会简要回顾改革的原因——我们确实需要彻底改变，才能重启增长。

lines.t: M: After that, I'll outline the new company structures and who's going where.
lines.cn: M：之后我会概述新的公司架构，以及谁去哪儿。

lines.t: M: Then, I'll hand it over to you to discuss the timeline and summarize, and we'll take questions together at the end.
lines.cn: M：然后交给你来讲时间安排并做总结，最后我们一起回答问题。

lines.t: F: Anything else?
lines.cn: F：还有别的吗？

lines.t: M: Oh, yeah.
lines.cn: M：哦，有。

lines.t: M: We should let the staff know the channels of communication, you know, who they can contact or direct questions to about these changes.
lines.cn: M：我们应该让员工知道沟通渠道，也就是关于这些变动他们可以联系谁、向谁提问。

lines.t: F: Yes.
lines.cn: F：对。

lines.t: M: And we can collect some frequently asked questions and present some general answers.
lines.cn: M：我们还可以收集一些常见问题，给出统一的回答。

lines.t: F: Hmm.
lines.cn: F：嗯。

lines.t: M: And we'll make the presentation and the questions available via the company's own computer network, right?
lines.cn: M：我们还会把演示和问题放到公司自己的内部网络上，对吧？

lines.t: F: Yes.
lines.cn: F：对。

lines.t: M: We'll make a page on the network where staff can download all the details.
lines.cn: M：我们会在内网上做一个页面，员工可以在那里下载全部细节。

lines.t: F: All right.
lines.cn: F：好的。

lines.t: F: Perhaps we should do a practice run of the presentation first?
lines.cn: F：也许我们应该先做一次演练？

lines.t: M: You bet.
lines.cn: M：当然。

questions.stem: What is special about the Cincinnati-Northern Kentucky International Airport?

options.A: It helps passengers to take care of their pet animals.
options.B: It has animals to help passengers carry their language.
options.C: It uses therapy animals to soothe nervous passengers.
options.D: It allows passengers to have animal travel with them.

questions.cn: 辛辛那提—北肯塔基国际机场有什么特别之处？

optionsCn.A: 它帮乘客照看宠物。
optionsCn.B: 它有动物帮乘客搬运行李。
optionsCn.C: 它用治疗动物来安抚紧张的乘客。
optionsCn.D: 它允许乘客带动物同行。

questions.stem: What are the trained animals probably capable of doing in an airport?

options.A: Avoiding possible dangers.
options.B: Finding their way around.
options.C: Identifying drug smugglers.
options.D: Looking after sick passengers.

questions.cn: 这些受过训练的动物在机场大概能做什么？

optionsCn.A: 避开可能的危险。
optionsCn.B: 在机场里认路。
optionsCn.C: 识别毒品走私者。
optionsCn.D: 照顾生病的乘客。

options.A: Schedule their flights around the animal visits.
options.B: Photograph the therapy animals at the airport.
options.C: Keep some animals for therapeutic purposes.
options.D: Bring their animals on board their plane.

questions.cn: 有些乘客会尝试做什么？

optionsCn.A: 把航班安排在动物到访的时间前后。
optionsCn.B: 在机场给治疗动物拍照。
optionsCn.C: 养一些动物用于治疗目的。
optionsCn.D: 把动物带上飞机。

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: Airline passengers have to deal with a lot these days, getting bumped from flights and losing luggage on top of the general anxiety that nervous passengers always feel.
lines.cn: 如今，航空乘客要应对的麻烦很多：除了紧张的乘客本就常有的普遍焦虑，还有被挤下航班、行李丢失。

lines.t: At the Cincinnati-Northern Kentucky International Airport, miniature horses deliver a calming force two times a month.
lines.cn: 在辛辛那提—北肯塔基国际机场，迷你马每月两次前来提供安抚力量。

lines.t: Denver and Ruby are two of the 34 therapy horses brought in from a local farm.
lines.cn: 丹佛和鲁比就是从当地农场带来的 34 匹治疗马中的两匹。

lines.t: They can usually be found in the ticket counter area, interacting with travelers.
lines.cn: 它们通常待在有值机柜台的区域，与旅客互动。

lines.t: More than 30 airports across the country now have therapy dogs.
lines.cn: 全美现在有 30 多个机场配备了治疗犬。

lines.t: San Francisco has a therapy pig.
lines.cn: 旧金山有一只治疗猪。

lines.t: San Jose, California, began a dog program after the terrorist attacks of September 11.
lines.cn: 加州圣何塞在 9·11 恐怖袭击之后启动了一个犬类项目。

lines.t: Since its beginning, the program has now grown and has 21 therapy dogs and a therapy cat.
lines.cn: 自开展以来，该项目不断壮大，如今已有 21 只治疗犬和一只治疗猫。

lines.t: The animals don't get startled.
lines.cn: 这些动物不会被吓到。

lines.t: They have had hundreds of hours of airport training, so they are used to having luggage and people crowding around them.
lines.cn: 它们接受过数百小时的机场训练，所以习惯了行李和人群围在身边。

lines.t: These professional animals are probably better at finding their way in the airports than the most frequent of travelers.
lines.cn: 这些专业动物在机场认路的本事，大概比最常飞的旅客还强。

lines.t: The passengers often say that seeing animals makes them feel much better and helps them to calm down before a flight.
lines.cn: 乘客常说，看到动物让他们感觉好多了，也有助于在登机前平静下来。

lines.t: This little bit of support can sometimes make a big difference.
lines.cn: 这点小小的支持，有时能带来很大的不同。

lines.t: Some passengers enjoy the animals so much that they call the airport to schedule flights around their visits.
lines.cn: 有些乘客太喜欢这些动物了，甚至打电话给机场，把航班安排在它们到访的时间前后。

lines.t: Visits to nursing homes and schools are also a regular part of the horses' schedule.
lines.cn: 探访养老院和学校也是这些马固定行程的一部分。

lines.t: Their owner is already working on a new idea for a therapy animal, donkeys.
lines.cn: 它们的主人已经在琢磨一种新的治疗动物——驴。

options.A: Beside a beautifully painted wall in Arles.
options.B: Beside the gate of an ancient Roman city.
options.C: At the site of an ancient Roman mansion.

questions.cn: 讲话者站在哪里？

optionsCn.A: 在阿尔勒一面精美彩绘墙旁。
optionsCn.B: 在一座古罗马城市的城门旁。
optionsCn.C: 在一座古罗马宅邸的遗址上。
optionsCn.D: 在罗马一处接待厅的入口。

questions.stem: What do the thousands of fragments display when they are put back together?

options.A: A number of different images.
options.B: A number of mythological heroes.
options.C: Various musical instruments.
options.D: Paintings by famous French artists.

questions.cn: 数千块碎片拼接起来后呈现出什么？

optionsCn.A: 许多不同的图案。
optionsCn.B: 许多神话英雄。
optionsCn.C: 各种各样的乐器。
optionsCn.D: 法国著名画家的画作。

questions.stem: What makes experts think the paintings were done by artists from Italy?

options.A: The originality and expertise shown.
options.B: The worldly sophistication displayed.
options.C: The stunning images vividly depicted.
options.D: The impressive skills and costly dyes.

questions.cn: 是什么让专家认为这些壁画出自意大利画师之手？

optionsCn.A: 所展现的独创性与专业水准。
optionsCn.B: 所展示的世俗见识与品位。
optionsCn.C: 所生动描绘的惊人图像。
optionsCn.D: 令人惊叹的技艺和昂贵的颜料。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the passage about the owner of the mansion?

options.A: His artistic taste is superb.
options.B: His identity remains unclear.
options.C: He was a collector of antiques.
options.D: He was a rich Italian merchant.

questions.cn: 从短文中我们了解到宅邸主人的什么情况？

optionsCn.A: 他的艺术品味极佳。
optionsCn.B: 他的身份仍不清楚。
optionsCn.C: 他是一位古董收藏家。
optionsCn.D: 他是一位富有的意大利商人。

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: Hello, viewers!
lines.cn: 观众朋友们，大家好！

lines.t: Today, I'm standing at a 2,000-year-old Roman-era site.
lines.cn: 今天，我站在一处有两千年历史的罗马时代遗址上。

lines.t: Here, the brightly colored scenes that once decorated a mansion are being dug up.
lines.cn: 在这里，曾经装饰一座宅邸的色彩鲜艳的壁画正被发掘出土。

lines.t: These scenes are turning up in the southern French city of Arles, surprising the historians who have been working here since 2014.
lines.cn: 这些壁画出现在法国南部城市阿尔勒，令自 2014 年以来一直在此工作的历史学家们感到惊讶。

lines.t: Patches of paint still cling to the stone walls of the bedroom and reception hall.
lines.cn: 卧室和接待厅的石墙上仍残留着一片片颜料。

lines.t: Some of these painted walls are preserved in places to a height of one meter.
lines.cn: 部分彩绘墙面在有些地方保存高度达一米。

lines.t: In addition, thousands of fragments that fell off the walls have been recovered.
lines.cn: 此外，还有数千块从墙上脱落的碎片被找回。

lines.t: These pieces have been put back together with great care and display a variety of images.
lines.cn: 这些碎片已被小心翼翼地重新拼接起来，呈现出各式各样的图案。

lines.t: Some of these images include figures never seen before in France, such as a woman playing a stringed instrument, possibly a character from mythology.
lines.cn: 其中一些图案包含法国前所未见的人物形象，比如一位弹奏弦乐器的女子，可能是神话中的人物。

lines.t: The paintings were done with such skill and with such expensive dyes that experts believe the artists originally came from Italy.
lines.cn: 这些壁画技艺如此高超、所用颜料如此昂贵，专家认为画师原本来自意大利。

lines.t: They were likely hired by one of the city's elite.
lines.cn: 他们很可能是受雇于该城的一位精英人物。

lines.t: Perhaps a Roman official wanted Pompeii-like interior to remind him of home.
lines.cn: 也许是一位罗马官员想要庞贝风格的室内装饰，以寄托思乡之情。

lines.t: He was probably stationed in this provincial trading port founded in 46 BC as a colony for veterans of the Roman army.
lines.cn: 他很可能是驻扎在这个行省贸易港的官员，该港建于公元前 46 年，是罗马军队老兵的聚居地。

lines.t: Or maybe a wealthy local wanted to show off his worldly sophistication.
lines.cn: 又或者是一位当地富人想炫耀自己的见识与品位。

lines.t: The paintings may yield even more stunning surprises as additional sections are put together like pieces of a puzzle.
lines.cn: 随着更多部分像拼图一样被拼接起来，这些壁画或许还会带来更惊人的惊喜。

lines.t: Whoever it was that created such magnificent pieces of art, they surely had no idea that their work would still be around thousands of years later.
lines.cn: 无论创作这些宏伟艺术品的是谁，他们肯定想不到自己的作品在数千年后依然存在。

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: Good afternoon class.
lines.cn: 同学们，下午好。

lines.t: Today I want to discuss with you a new approach to empirical research.
lines.cn: 今天我想和大家讨论实证研究的一种新路径。

lines.t: In the past, scientists often worked alone.
lines.cn: 过去，科学家往往独自工作。

lines.t: They were confined to the university or research center where they worked.
lines.cn: 他们被局限在自己工作的大学或研究中心里。

lines.t: Today, though, we are seeing mergers of some of the greatest scientific minds, regardless of their location.
lines.cn: 但如今，我们看到一些最杰出的科学头脑正在联合起来，不论他们身处何地。

lines.t: There has never been a better time for collaborations with foreign scientists.
lines.cn: 与外国科学家合作，从未有过比现在更好的时机。

lines.t: In fact, the European Union is taking the lead.
lines.cn: 事实上，欧盟正走在前列。

lines.t: Spurred on by funding policies, half of European research articles had international co-authors in 2007.
lines.cn: 在资助政策的推动下，2007 年欧洲有一半的研究论文拥有国际合著者。

lines.t: This is more than twice the level of two decades ago.
lines.cn: 这是二十年前水平的两倍多。

lines.t: The European Union's level of international co-authorship is about twice that of the United States, Japan and India.
lines.cn: 欧盟的国际合著比例约为美国、日本和印度的两倍。

lines.t: Even so, the levels in these countries are also rising.
lines.cn: 即便如此，这些国家的比例也在上升。

lines.t: This is a sign of the continued allure of creating scientific coalitions across borders.
lines.cn: 这表明跨国组建科学联盟仍有持续的吸引力。

lines.t: Andras Schubert, a researcher at the Institute for Science Policy Research, says that the rise in collaboration is partly out of necessity.
lines.cn: 科学政策研究所的研究员安德拉什·舒伯特说，合作的增加部分出于必要。

lines.t: This necessity comes with the rise of big science.
lines.cn: 这种必要性伴随着“大科学”的兴起而来。

lines.t: Many scientific endeavors have become more complicated.
lines.cn: 许多科学探索变得更加复杂。

lines.t: These new complications require the money and labor of many nations.
lines.cn: 这些新的复杂问题需要许多国家的资金和人力。

lines.t: But, he says, collaborations have also emerged because of increased possibilities.
lines.cn: 不过他说，合作的出现也因为可能性增多了。

lines.t: The Internet allows like-minded scientists to find each other.
lines.cn: 互联网让志同道合的科学家得以彼此结识。

lines.t: Simultaneously, dramatic drops in communication costs ease long-distance interactions.
lines.cn: 与此同时，通信成本的急剧下降也便利了远距离交流。

lines.t: And there's a reward.
lines.cn: 而且还有回报。

lines.t: Studies of citation counts show that internationally co-authored papers have better visibility.
lines.cn: 对引用次数的研究表明，国际合作署名的论文有更高的可见度。

lines.t: Schubert says international collaboration is a way to spread ideas in wider and wider circles.
lines.cn: 舒伯特说，国际合作是把思想传播到越来越广范围的一种方式。

lines.t: Caroline Wagner, a research scientist at George Washington University, notes that international collaborations offer additional flexibility.
lines.cn: 乔治·华盛顿大学的研究科学家卡罗琳·瓦格纳指出，国际合作提供了额外的灵活性。

lines.t: Whereas local collaborations sometimes persist past the point of usefulness because of social or academic obligations, international ones can be cultivated and dropped more freely.
lines.cn: 国内的合作为了社会或学术上的义务，有时会在失去价值后仍继续维持，而国际合作则可以更自由地建立和结束。

lines.t: The collaborative trend is true across scientific disciplines.
lines.cn: 这种合作趋势在各个科学学科中都存在。

lines.t: Some fields, though, have a greater tendency for it.
lines.cn: 不过有些领域更倾向于合作。

lines.t: Particle physicists and astronomers collaborate often.
lines.cn: 粒子物理学家和天文学家经常合作。

lines.t: This is because they must share expensive facilities.
lines.cn: 这是因为他们必须共用昂贵的设施。

lines.t: Mathematicians, by contrast, tend historically towards solitude.
lines.cn: 相比之下，数学家在历史上倾向于独自研究。

lines.t: As a consequence, they lag behind other disciplines.
lines.cn: 结果，他们落后于其他学科。

lines.t: However, Wagner says, partnerships are rising there, too.
lines.cn: 不过瓦格纳说，这一领域的合作也在增加。

lines.t: The level of collaboration also varies from country to country.
lines.cn: 合作的程度也因国家而异。

lines.t: There are historical and political reasons as to why collaborations emerge, says Wagner.
lines.cn: 瓦格纳说，合作的出现有其历史和政治原因。

lines.t: This rise is also apparently boosted by policies embedded in European framework funding schemes.
lines.cn: 这一增长显然也得益于欧洲框架资助计划中所包含的政策。

lines.t: These policies underlie funding requirements that often require teamwork.
lines.cn: 这些政策构成了资助要求的基础，而这些要求往往需要团队协作。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: Good evening.
lines.cn: 晚上好。

lines.t: In 1959, on the day that I was born, a headline in Life magazine proclaimed, Target Venus.
lines.cn: 1959 年，就在我出生的那天，《生活》杂志的一个标题宣告：“目标金星”。

lines.t: There may be life there.
lines.cn: 那里可能有生命。

lines.t: It told of how scientists rode a balloon to an altitude of 80,000 feet to make telescope observations of Venus' atmosphere and how their discovery of water raised hopes that there could be living things there.
lines.cn: 文章讲述了科学家们如何乘气球升到 8 万英尺高空，用望远镜观测金星大气，以及他们发现水如何燃起了那里或许存在生命的希望。

lines.t: As a kid, I thrilled to tales of adventure in Isaac Asimov's juvenile science fiction novel Lucky Star and the Oceans of Venus.
lines.cn: 小时候，艾萨克·阿西莫夫的少年科幻小说《幸运星与金星之海》里的冒险故事让我兴奋不已。

lines.t: For many of my peers, though, Venus quickly lost its romance.
lines.cn: 不过对我的许多同龄人来说，金星很快就失去了浪漫色彩。

lines.t: The very first thing that scientists discovered with a mission to another planet was that Venus was not at all the earthly paradise that fiction had portrayed.
lines.cn: 科学家们首次探测另一颗行星时发现的第一件事就是：金星根本不是科幻作品描绘的人间天堂。

lines.t: It is nearly identical to our own planet in bulk properties such as mass, density, and size, but its surface has been cooked and dried by an ocean of carbon dioxide.
lines.cn: 它的质量、密度和大小等整体属性与我们的地球几乎相同，但其表面已被二氧化碳的“海洋”烘烤干涸。

lines.t: Trapped in the burning death grip of a runaway greenhouse effect, Venus has long been held up as a cautionary tale for everything that could go wrong on a planet like Earth.
lines.cn: 金星被困在失控温室效应炽热的死亡之握中，长期以来被当作警示案例，说明像地球这样的行星可能出的各种问题。

lines.t: As a possible home for alien life, it has been voted the planet least likely to succeed.
lines.cn: 作为外星生命可能的家园，它被评为最不可能成功的行星。

lines.t: But I have refused to give up on Venus, and over the years my stubborn loyalty has been justified.
lines.cn: 但我一直拒绝对金星死心，而多年来，我这份固执的忠诚被证明是有道理的。

lines.t: The rocky views glimpsed by Venera 9 and other Russian landers suggested a tortured volcanic history.
lines.cn: “金星 9 号”及其他俄罗斯着陆器瞥见的岩石景象，暗示着一段剧烈动荡的火山历史。

lines.t: That was confirmed in the early 1990s by the American Magellan orbiter, which used radar to peer through the planet's thick clouds and map out a rich, varied, and dynamic surface.
lines.cn: 这一点在 20 世纪 90 年代初得到美国“麦哲伦号”环金轨道的证实，它用雷达穿透金星浓密的云层，绘制出丰富多样、动态变化的地表。

lines.t: The surface formed mostly in the last billion years, which makes it fresher and more recently active than any rocky planet other than Earth.
lines.cn: 其地表主要形成于过去十亿年间，因此比除地球以外的任何岩石行星都更年轻、更晚近仍有活动。

lines.t: Russian and American spacecraft also found hints that its ancient climate might have been wetter, cooler, and possibly even friendly to life.
lines.cn: 俄罗斯和美国的航天器还发现了线索，暗示金星古代气候可能更湿润、更凉爽，甚至可能适宜生命。

lines.t: Measurements of density and composition imply that Venus originally formed out of basically the same stuff as Earth.
lines.cn: 对密度和成分的测量表明，金星最初与地球由基本相同的物质构成。

lines.t: That presumably included much more water than the tiny trace we find blowing in the thick air today.
lines.cn: 那其中想必包含的水，远比我们今天在浓厚大气中探测到的微量要多得多。

lines.t: Thus our picture of Venus at around the time life was getting started on Earth is one of warm oceans, probably rich with organic molecules, splashing around rocky shores and volcanic vents.
lines.cn: 因此，在地球生命刚刚起步的那个时期，我们描绘的金星图景是：温暖的海洋，可能富含有机分子，在岩石海岸和火山口周围拍打翻涌。

lines.t: The sun was considerably less bright back then, so Venus was arguably a cozier habitat for life than Earth.
lines.cn: 那时的太阳比现在暗得多，因此可以说金星是比地球更舒适的宜居环境。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: I'm a psychology professor at the University of British Columbia.
lines.cn: 我是英属哥伦比亚大学的心理学教授。

lines.t: I specialize in cultural psychology, examining similarities and differences between East Asians and North Americans.
lines.cn: 我专攻文化心理学，研究东亚人与北美人的相似与差异。

lines.t: Our research team has been looking at cultural differences in self-enhancing motivations, how people have positive feelings towards not only themselves, but things connected to themselves.
lines.cn: 我们的研究团队一直在研究自我提升动机上的文化差异，即人们不仅对自己、也对自己相关的事物抱有积极情感的方式。

lines.t: For example, when you own something, you view it as more valuable than when you don't own it.
lines.cn: 比如，当你拥有某样东西时，你会觉得它比不拥有时更有价值。

lines.t: It's called the endowment effect.
lines.cn: 这叫做禀赋效应。

lines.t: The strength of that effect is stronger in Western cultures than in East Asian cultures.
lines.cn: 这种效应的强度在西方文化中比在东亚文化中更强。

lines.t: So we've been looking at other ways of seeing whether this motivation to view oneself positively is shaped by cultural experiences.
lines.cn: 所以我们一直在寻找其他途径，来检验这种积极看待自己的动机是否由文化经历塑造。

lines.t: We've also started to look at how culture shapes sleep.
lines.cn: 我们还开始研究文化如何塑造睡眠。

lines.t: We are still in the exploratory stages of this project, although what's noteworthy is that East Asians on average sleep about an hour and a half less each night than North Americans do.
lines.cn: 这个项目仍处于探索阶段，不过值得注意的是，东亚人平均每晚比北美人少睡约一个半小时。

lines.t: And it's not a more efficient sleep, not like they're compressing relatively more value out of their hours.
lines.cn: 而且这并不是更高效的睡眠，并不是说他们从这些小时里榨取了相对更多的价值。

lines.t: Other studies have found that even infants in East Asia sleep about an hour less than European infants.
lines.cn: 其他研究发现，东亚的婴儿甚至比欧洲婴儿少睡约一小时。

lines.t: So we're trying to figure out how culture shapes the way you sleep.
lines.cn: 所以我们正试图弄清文化如何塑造人的睡眠方式。

lines.t: Our experiment does not take place in a sleep lab.
lines.cn: 我们的实验不在睡眠实验室里进行。

lines.t: Instead, we lend people motion-detecting watches and they wear them for a week at a time.
lines.cn: 而是把运动监测手表借给受试者，让他们一次佩戴一周。

lines.t: Whenever they are not having a shower or swimming, they keep it on.
lines.cn: 只要不是在洗澡或游泳，他们就一直戴着。

lines.t: These kinds of watches are used in sleep studies as a way of measuring how long people are sleeping, how efficient their sleep is, and whether they are waking up in the night.
lines.cn: 这类手表在睡眠研究中用于测量人们睡了多久、睡眠效率如何，以及夜间是否醒来。

lines.t: Ideally, I'd like to take this into a controlled lab environment.
lines.cn: 理想情况下，我希望把这项研究带入可控的实验室环境。

lines.t: We'll see where the research points us.
lines.cn: 我们且看研究会把我们引向何方。

lines.t: We usually start off with the more affordable methods.
lines.cn: 我们通常从成本较低的方法开始。

lines.t: And if everything looks promising, then it'll justify trying to build a sleep lab and study sleep across cultures that way.
lines.cn: 如果一切看起来有希望，那就值得尝试建一个睡眠实验室，用那种方式跨文化地研究睡眠。

lines.t: Why do we study sleep?
lines.cn: 我们为什么研究睡眠？

lines.t: Sleep is something that has really been an unexplored topic cross-culturally.
lines.cn: 睡眠确实是一个在跨文化层面尚未被探索的课题。

lines.t: I'm attracted to it because culture isn't something that only shapes the way our minds operate.
lines.cn: 它吸引我，是因为文化并不只塑造我们思维的运作方式。

lines.t: It shapes the way our bodies operate, too, and sleep is at the intersection of those.
lines.cn: 它也塑造我们身体的运作方式，而睡眠正处于两者的交汇点上。
